purpose: Macro Event & Surprise Foundation: establish a PIT-correct record of what macro event was scheduled, what the pre-release market consensus was (and exactly when that consensus snapshot was observed), what was FIRST released, what 'previous' value was shown as published at that time, and how surprise is calculated per explicit event dimension. v1 scope is narrow: CPI (simple numeric release) and FOMC (multi-dimensional event, each dimension receiving its own independent surprise, never a single aggregate score). This is measurement infrastructure only -- MACRO MEASUREMENT FIRST, MACRO FORECASTING LATER. No proprietary macro forecast, no cross-asset transmission, no causal claims, no company exposure, no valuation changes, no expected return. See forbidden_actions for the full list of prohibited out-of-scope operations for this task; those are constraints on the executor, not requests.
requested_actions: implement Japanese_Equity_Lab/lib/macro_events/model.py providing MacroEvent (historically identifiable event occurrence, v1 scope restricted to CPI/FOMC event types via SUPPORTED_EVENT_TYPES), MacroConsensusSnapshot (always tied to an explicit consensus_snapshot_at, never overwritten, multiple snapshots per event/dimension coexist independently), and MacroFirstRelease (the historically-first-published value and previous-as-published value, with no update/revise method -- later revisions must be a separate future record, never a mutation of this one) -- a new independent namespace (lib/macro_events/) distinct from the existing lib/macro/ package (Series-centric long-form macro observation with RevisionHistory-based vintage tracking, a different shape/purpose that is not reused or modified)

implement Japanese_Equity_Lab/lib/macro_events/surprise.py providing compute_macro_surprise() as the sole entrypoint computing one MacroSurprise per (event, dimension, consensus_snapshot, first_release) tuple -- never an aggregate/opaque score across dimensions -- enforcing the consensus PIT rule (consensus_snapshot_at < actual_public_at AND consensus.available_at <= actual_public_at), explicit per-dimension calculation rules (CALC_RULE_ACTUAL_MINUS_EXPECTED_PP_V1 for percentage-point differences, CALC_RULE_ACTUAL_MINUS_EXPECTED_BP_V1 for basis-point-converted rate decisions) with strict unit validation and no implicit conversion

implement Japanese_Equity_Lab/lib/macro_events/store.py reusing the existing generic lib.evaluation.store.AppendOnlyRecordStore (no new persistence mechanism) with factory functions for all four record types, preserving the unconditional reject-on-duplicate-ID policy
reuse lib.evaluation.integrity.compute_record_hash()/verify_record_integrity() for tamper evidence on every new record type (no new hash algorithm)

add unit tests in Japanese_Equity_Lab/13_tests/test_macro_event_surprise.py covering the CPI acceptance scenario (Section 27: two differently-timed consensus snapshots coexisting, producing two distinct correctly-valued surprises), the FOMC acceptance scenario (Section 28: two independent dimension surprises, no aggregate), and Required Tests Sections 29-32 (identity/immutability, PIT, surprise computation, historical fidelity)
run ruff check/format and mypy --strict on the three new lib/macro_events/*.py files
run the targeted pytest suite for test_macro_event_surprise.py, then the D0102-D0110.1 + existing lib/macro regression suite, then the full repository pytest suite
record the design decision in DECISIONS.md
